name: reaction-diffusion
title: Turing patterns: Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion (headline)
question:
Do three independently-authored processes -- TWO ``DiffusionProcess``
instances (one per species, U at Du and V at Dv=Du/2, each with no
knowledge of reactions) and ONE ``GrayScottReactionProcess`` (no knowledge
of FEM/diffusion) -- produce a genuine 2D Turing instability when wired to
the same bigraph stores: does a near-uniform field spontaneously
self-organize into spots/stripes/labyrinth patterns, with none of the
three processes calling into either of the others?
hypothesis:
Coupling is entirely a property of the document wiring (shared
``stores.u`` / ``stores.v`` / ``stores.source_u`` / ``stores.source_v``
paths), not of any one process's implementation: starting from U~1, V~0
everywhere plus a small seeded perturbation, the differential diffusion
(Du > Dv) between the two DiffusionProcess instances, combined with the
GrayScottReactionProcess's nonlinear feed/kill kinetics, should amplify
the perturbation into a spatially heterogeneous, bounded pattern -- not
decay back to uniformity, and not blow up -- and different (F, k) kinetic
parameters should produce visibly different pattern morphologies.
objective:
Run the ``turing_patterns`` composite (2x DiffusionProcess ⊕
GrayScottReactionProcess) across three Gray-Scott parameter regimes and
confirm (a) the baseline regime's V field grows substantially more
spatially heterogeneous over the run (pattern EMERGES from a near-uniform
start), (b) the resulting pattern is bounded and structurally
non-trivial -- a finite fraction of the domain organizes into pattern
features, not the whole domain and not none of it -- and (c) different
(F, k) regimes produce measurably different pattern morphology (coverage
fraction), demonstrating the composed system is a genuine, tunable Turing
system, not a fixed numerical artifact.
description:
This is the investigation's headline composability + visual showcase.
``DiffusionProcess`` is instantiated TWICE -- once per species, with
differential diffusivities Du=2e-5 (species U) and Dv=1e-5=Du/2 (species
V), the classic Gray-Scott ratio that permits a Turing instability -- and
coupled to a single ``GrayScottReactionProcess`` purely through shared
stores: ``stores.u`` is read+written by the U-diffusion process and read
by the reaction process; ``stores.v`` is read+written by the V-diffusion
process and read by the reaction process; ``stores.source_u`` /
``stores.source_v`` are written by the reaction process
(``overwrite[array[float]]`` -- fresh per-tick rates, not accumulated
deltas) and read by the matching diffusion process, which multiplies its
own species' rate by dt internally. None of the three processes is aware
of the other two, or of Gray-Scott as a system -- the PDE
``dU/dt = Du*lap(U) - U*V^2 + F*(1-U)``, ``dV/dt = Dv*lap(V) + U*V^2 -
(F+k)*V`` emerges purely from the document wiring, extending
``reaction_diffusion``'s two-process Fisher-KPP coupling (Task 3/4) to a
genuinely three-process, two-species system whose only route to
pattern-forming AT ALL is that three-way coupling.

Regime note (from development): the textbook "spots" Gray-Scott regime
(F=0.035, k=0.065) was tried first and found SUBCRITICAL for this
composite's Du/Dv/dt/domain-size combination -- every seeding strategy
tried (a localized central patch alone, the patch plus whole-field noise,
patch sizes up to 0.3 of the domain) decayed back to the trivial (U=1,
V=0) fixed point within a few hundred ticks instead of nucleating. This is
real reaction-diffusion physics (a perturbation below the local
autocatalytic threshold decays exponentially via the reaction's own
linear term once diffusion dilutes it enough), not a bug -- see the
study's report for the calibration sweep. Three other well-known Pearson
(1993) regimes were verified to grow robustly under the same conditions
and are used instead: the baseline (F=0.037, k=0.06, this composite's own
default parameters) sits in the same "coral / dividing-spots" family as
the classic "mitosis" regime; the two variants are a labyrinth regime
(F=0.03, k=0.06) and a stripes/worms regime (F=0.055, k=0.062).

Initial condition (``_gray_scott_seed`` in
``viva_fenics.composites.turing_patterns``): U=1, V=0 everywhere except a
small central square seeded to U~0.5, V~0.25, PLUS tiny noise added to
every node (not just the seeded patch) -- empirically required to
reliably nucleate a pattern rather than have the single localized
perturbation diffuse away before the reaction can amplify it (standard
practice for Gray-Scott initial conditions; the PDE/coefficients
themselves are unchanged).

Achieved result (the committed run, extended from an earlier onset-only
sizing to reach mature texture -- ~2.7h total wall-time across all three
regimes): the baseline (coral/mitosis-like, resolution=128, 18000
backward-Euler ticks) self-organized from a near-uniform start into a
10.2x var(V) growth, settling into a single connected pattern region
covering 48.0% of the domain (bounded, no blow-up). The labyrinth variant
(resolution=96, 10000 ticks) grew 10.5x and, distinctively, has matured
into a genuine labyrinth: 40 disconnected regions (coverage 30.1%) -- up
from ~9 regions at the earlier, shorter sizing -- a clearly different,
now visually unambiguous "labyrinth" topology vs. the single-blob
baseline/stripes. The stripes/worms variant (resolution=96, 10000 ticks)
grew 15.5x to 49.7% coverage, still a single connected region at this
tick count. The three regimes' coverage spans 0.301-0.497 (spread 0.196)
-- driven by both the (F, k) kinetics and (to a lesser extent than
before) the variants' still-coarser-than-baseline mesh; the labyrinth's
40-vs-1 blob-count difference remains the cleanest topological signal
that (F, k) genuinely changes pattern structure, not just its extent.
This extended run reaches materially more mature texture than the
earlier onset-only sizing (most visibly the labyrinth's blob count
jumping from ~9 to 40), though it is still a finite-time snapshot, not an
infinite-time steady state -- see the study's report for the full
breakdown.

expected_behavior.name: pattern-emerges
expected_behavior.en: V's spatial variance grows at least 5x over the baseline run, i.e. the field self-organizes away from its near-uniform start.
expected_behavior.condition: var(V, final) >= 5x var(V, initial), baseline regime
expected_behavior.rationale: The seeded initial condition already has a nonzero variance (the central patch plus whole-field noise); a bare "variance increases" check would also pass on quadrature noise alone. Requiring at least 5x growth over the full run distinguishes genuine reaction-diffusion self-organization from residual solver noise -- see this study's report for the achieved value.

expected_behavior.name: pattern-structured-not-blowup
expected_behavior.en: The baseline pattern's fraction of the domain 'inside' a pattern feature lands in a finite, non-degenerate band, and every field stays within a physically-sane range.
expected_behavior.condition: 0.1 <= coverage <= 0.7, and U/V in (-0.5, 1.5) throughout every regime
expected_behavior.rationale: A coverage near 0 means the pattern never really emerged (still essentially the tiny seed); a coverage near 1 means the whole domain saturated (not a spatially structured pattern, or a numerical blow-up masquerading as one). The field-range check independently guards against the accumulate-vs-overwrite regression class (the source stores composing additively instead of being overwritten each tick), which blows fields well past this band.

expected_behavior.name: regimes-differ
expected_behavior.en: The three (F, k) regimes produce measurably different pattern coverage -- different kinetics give qualitatively different morphology, not the same pattern relabeled.
expected_behavior.rationale: If every regime produced statistically indistinguishable coverage, the (F, k) parameters would not be doing meaningful kinetic work -- the "tunable Turing system" claim would be unsupported. A real spread demonstrates the composed system's morphology genuinely depends on the reaction kinetics, as Gray-Scott theory predicts. (The labyrinth regime's connected-component count, 9 vs the other two regimes' 1, is an even sharper topological signal of the same claim -- see the study's report -- but coverage is the metric this test gates on since it is defined and computed identically for every regime.)

behavior_tests.name: pattern-emerges
behavior_tests.description:
var(V) at the end of the baseline run must be at least 5x var(V) at the
start.

provenance.note: The committed extended production run (resolution=128, 18000 ticks, dt=1.0) achieved growth=10.2x; 5.0 leaves ~2x headroom below that while still catching a "reaction never actually coupled in" regression (which produces order-1 growth from quadrature noise alone, per the analogous check in ``reaction_diffusion``'s Fisher-KPP study).

behavior_tests.name: pattern-structured-not-blowup
behavior_tests.description:
The baseline's final-V coverage fraction (see ``_pattern_metrics`` in
``sims/run.py``) must land in [0.1, 0.7], and every regime's final
U/V fields must stay within (-0.5, 1.5).

provenance.note: The committed extended production run's baseline achieved coverage=0.480 (comfortably bounded, no blow-up); [0.1, 0.7] brackets that with headroom on both sides while still catching "pattern never really emerged" (near 0) or "whole domain saturated/blew up" (near 1). The field-bound half of this check mirrors the FAST unit tests' (-0.5, 1.5) band, itself the accumulate-vs-overwrite regression guard (see ``tests/test_turing_patterns.py``).

behavior_tests.name: regimes-differ
behavior_tests.description:
max(coverage) - min(coverage) across the baseline + 2 variant regimes
must be at least 0.1.

provenance.note: The committed extended production run achieved coverage 0.480 (baseline) / 0.301 (labyrinth) / 0.497 (stripes) -- a spread of 0.196. 0.1 leaves ~2x headroom below that while still catching a "regimes don't actually differ" regression. Coverage is still partly confounded by the labyrinth/stripes variants running at a coarser mesh than the baseline (an explicit, disclosed wall-time tradeoff -- see the study report); the labyrinth regime's connected-component count (40, vs 1 for the other two regimes) is a second, less-confounded topological signal of the same claim, not gated on here only because it isn't defined identically enough across regimes for a clean numeric threshold.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
No further studies in this investigation depend on reaction-diffusion --
it is the investigation's headline/terminal study, demonstrating the
composability + visual claim the other studies build up to.
